Subject: Private/Dedicated capacity planning 

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. HorizonBio is ready to move from eval to a committed capacity conversation. High level asks: we need a MAP that captures evaluation milestones, procurement/lead times for Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem), and an acceptance window that aligns with our internal validation cadence.

Target: production traffic by late Q3. Our team will run two parallel eval tracks (functional + perf). Key constraints: vendor procurement (PO approvals) and a SOC2 audit scheduled in July that may influence acceptance gating.

Can you share a MAP draft that calls out realistic lead times for GPU pools (H100-equivalent) and recommended pool sizing for our projected peak Q4 requests? If you can include acceptance window options (standard vs accelerated) and implications for billing/credits, that would be very helpful.

Emily Park

HorizonBio

Emily — thanks, this is helpful. I put together a draft MAP and a lightweight capacity-sizing model so we can iterate quickly. Attaching: HZN-4782_MAP_v1.pdf and capacity_sizing_model_HZN-4782.xlsx.

High level summary here so you have it in the thread:
- Lead times (approx): Dedicated reserved H100-equivalent pool: 8–10 weeks lead from signed commitment to stable provision.
- Private (VPC managed by Redwood): 6–8 weeks if using our cloud region hosting; on-prem installations vary 12+ weeks depending on facility readiness and onsite networking.
- Pool sizing: we modeled three banded options (conservative/moderate/aggressive). For your Q4 peak estimate, moderate (24 x H100-equivalent) provides a ~2.5x buffer against forecasted concurrency; aggressive (48) reduces tail latency but increases committed cost.
- Acceptance window options: Standard = 6 weeks from provision to final acceptance (recommended for enterprises with audits); Accelerated = 3 weeks with an elevated acceptance support SLA and a small onboarding credit if acceptance completes <3 weeks.

Proposed MAP milestones (draft):
1) MAP sign: mutual sign-off of milestones and lead times (this doc)
2) Eval close: performance gate (2-week perf run)
3) Commit & PO: purchase order and SOW executed
4) Provisioning start: infra ordering / region allocation
5) Staging validation: customer runbook + 1-week smoke and perf tests
6) Acceptance: final sign-off and billing transition

Can we schedule a 30-min walkthrough next week? Monday/Tuesday morning PT works for me.

Thanks — attaching the draft for your legal/procurement review as well.

—Karthik

Karthik — quick thoughts after reviewing the workbook:

- Pool sizing: 24x H100-equivalent (moderate) is reasonable given their forecast. We should recommend a 3-stage rollout: 12 -> 24 -> 36 over 8 weeks post-provisioning to smooth costs and validate concurrency behavior.
- Lead times: confirm Dedicated reserved pool 8–10 weeks. For Private VPC we can hit 6 weeks if their account and network approvals are ready; recommend adding a 2-week staging buffer for SOC2-related validation.
- Accelerated acceptance: offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of first-month committed dollars if they choose the 3-week acceptance window and sign a dedicated onboarding SLA. That compensates for ops intensity.
- Procurement risks: call out rack-space & on-prem cabling (if they choose on-prem) as the primary reasons for 12+ week variability. If vendor logistics (Rajesh) can pre-commit cables and rack install windows, we can shave ~2 weeks.

Attachments: Updated sizing tab (embedded in the workbook). I recommend we reflect the staged rollout in the MAP and flag SOC2 as a conditional gating item.

Marissa
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
